## `policy-editor macos-applications`

Retrieves a list of applications for the specified policy, filtered by the provided application group and application criteria.

```
epm-cli policy-editor macos-applications <POLICYID> [flags]
```

API: `GET /PolicyEditor/v3/Policy/{policyId}/MacOS/ApplicationGroups` · Response: `MacPolicyApplicationGroupModel`

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<POLICYID>` | The unique identifier of the policy. |

**Filters and parameters**

| Flag | Type | Values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--application-group-name` | string |  | Filters on the application group using a StartsWith match. |
| `--application-group-id` | UUID |  | Filters on the unique identifier of the application group using an Exact match. |
| `--application-description` | string |  | Filters on the application description using a StartsWith match. |
| `--application-id` | UUID |  | Filters on the unique identifier of the application using an Exact match. |

**Example**

```sh
epm-cli policy-editor macos-applications <POLICYID> -o json
```

## `policy-editor macos-applications-modify`

Create, delete applications within application groups in a specified policy for a MacOS Policy.

To update an existing application in the policy, first use the DELETE endpoint to remove the current application, then use the CREATE endpoint to add the updated version. Supported application types for creation: bin, bund, pkg, scr, sudo, pref. To include a backslash in a string field, type \ twice (\\\\).

```
epm-cli policy-editor macos-applications-modify <POLICYID> [flags]
```

API: `POST /PolicyEditor/v3/Policy/{policyId}/MacOS/ApplicationGroups/Applications` · Response: `PolicyApplicationModified`

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<POLICYID>` | Policy Id |

**Request body** (JSON, `CreateMacOSUpdateDeleteApplicationRequest`)

Other or nested fields: `--set path=value`, or pass the whole body with `--body` (inline, `@file.json` or `-` for stdin). Example body (`--body-template`):

```json
{
  "applicationData": {
    "applicationGroups": {
      "edit": [
        {
          "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
          "applications": {
            "add": [
              null
            ],
            "delete": [
              null
            ]
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

**Example**

```sh
epm-cli policy-editor macos-applications-modify <POLICYID> --body @body.json
```

## `policy-editor windows-applications-modify`

Create, delete applications within application groups in a specified policy for a Windows policy.

To update an existing application in the policy, first use the DELETE endpoint to remove the current application, then use the CREATE endpoint to add the updated version. Supported application types for creation: bat, com, cpl, exe, msc, msi, ps1, reg, rpsc, rpss, unex, wsh. Unsupported application types for creation: ocx, svc, appx, unin (will not be supported in the future), dll, cont. Unsupported Matchers are: ActiveXCodebase, MaxVersion, MinVersion, ServiceConfigure, ServiceDisplayName, ServiceName, WindowsStorePackageName, WindowsStorePublisher To include a backslash in a string field, type \ twice (\\\\).

```
epm-cli policy-editor windows-applications-modify <POLICYID> [flags]
```

API: `POST /PolicyEditor/v3/Policy/{policyId}/Windows/ApplicationGroups/Applications` · Response: `PolicyApplicationModified`

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<POLICYID>` | Policy Id |

**Request body** (JSON, `CreateUpdateDeleteApplicationRequest`)

Other or nested fields: `--set path=value`, or pass the whole body with `--body` (inline, `@file.json` or `-` for stdin). Example body (`--body-template`):

```json
{
  "applicationData": {
    "applicationGroups": {
      "edit": [
        {
          "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
          "applications": {
            "add": [
              null
            ],
            "delete": [
              null
            ]
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

**Example**

```sh
epm-cli policy-editor windows-applications-modify <POLICYID> --body @body.json
```
